s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory failure with mediastinal mass and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: Dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Acute worsening of dyspnea leading to respiratory failure
Mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea
Pleural component with mass effect on surrounding structures
key_facts: 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion and intermittent dry cough
Hyporexia and unquantified intermittent fever
Delayed care until acute worsening of dyspnea
Developed acute respiratory failure and pulseless electrical activity arrest
Required orotracheal intubation and stabilization
Blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 16 bpm
Oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support
Anisocoria, jugular venous distension, sinus tachycardia, and bilateral coarse rales
Homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass on chest radiography
Lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura on CT scan
Pneumomediastinum, left pneumothorax, and lytic destruction of T1 and T2 vertebrae
WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL, hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL, platelets 303 × 10^3/µL
Elevated lactic acid, C-reactive protein, and LDH

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and acute respiratory failure

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and multiple organ involvement

shortlist.label: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and aggressive clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and potential for local invasion

shortlist.label: Thymic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive clinical presentation and mediastinal mass

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura, compressing and displacing the trachea, and causing respiratory symptoms, is consistent with primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. The mass effect on the right hilum, supra-aortic vessels, and superior vena cava, as well as the presence of pneumomediastinum, left pneumothorax, and lytic destruction of T1 and T2 vertebrae, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: Less likely due to the absence of characteristic Hodgkin lymphoma symptoms and the presence of a large, lobulated solid mass

rejected.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: Too broad a category, primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a well-defined, encapsulated mass in the anterior mediastinum, which is not consistent with the patient's imaging findings

rejected.label: Thymic carcinoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more aggressive clinical course and metastatic disease, which is not evident in the patient's presentation
